recipes.name: Mashed Jalapeño Cilantro Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_raw: sea salt and cracked black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bake sweet potatoes directly on the middle rack in the preheated oven until tender, 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Meanwhile, place jalapeño pepper directly on the middle rack with the potatoes in the oven and bake until the skin loosens, about 20 minutes. Peel jalapeño pepper, mince, and place into a large bowl.

Peel sweet potatoes and add to minced jalapeño pepper in the bowl. Add softened butter, orange juice, and cilantro. Mix with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy; season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a 1-quart baking dish. Drizzle with melted butter, then sprinkle the top with walnut pieces.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot in the center, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mashed Jalapeño Cilantro Sweet Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Roasted sweet potato and jalapeño pepper mix with fresh cilantro, butter, and orange juice for a delicious Texas-inspired side dish.

review.reviewBody: Awesome! Even my husband liked these and he isn't the biggest sweet potato fan. The only changes I made were to top with pecans instead of walnuts, cut the butter in half during the mashing step, and omitted the melted butter at the end. I suspected that all that butter wasn't totally necessary and I was right (at least for our tastes). Don't skip roasting the jalapeno, it gives the potatoes such a great flavor. Thanks!

We made this on our camping trip. I just cooked the sweet potatoes in the campfire wrapped in foil for about 50 min. Also roasted the jalapeno over the fire. I then mashed all the ingredients together except the orange juice, didn't have any and really don't think it was needed or we'd like that addition. Also didn't top with walnuts. These were very good and a nice change from regular grilled sweet potatoes, love the roasted jalapeno and sweet potato combo.

These are amazing!!! I've gotten really tired of the typical sweet potato dishes that are overly sweet and mixed with brown sugar, spices, etc. It's fine for Thanksgiving, but when it comes to summer, I want something with a fresh and bright flavor. This recipe totally fits the bill! I admit, I was running short on time, so I microwaved the potatoes on high for 6 minutes. I used the juice of one small orange. I mashed everything together and that was it. Time to dig in! I didn't bother drizzling the extra butter over top and baking in the oven. I also didn't use the walnut pieces, only because I didn't have any, but I'm sure it's quite tasty! The jalapeno really mellows as it roasts, so don't be afraid of using the whole pepper. Next time I will use two! I will also double the recipe. This is a keeper!

These were so good! I'll admit that I peeled and chopped the potatoes raw and microwaved them instead of baking them with the raw jalapeno already chopped with them, and I threw in two cloves of garlic. I thought that the OJ really gave them a brightness and I'll definitely make them again!

So good, yum! I added extra jalapenos and cilantro and omitted the walnuts, but I think it would be good with them next time.

Hubby doesn't usually care for sweet potato recipes because they're overly sweet, but he loved this. And so did I! Next time I will double the recipe. Thanks for sharing.

Wow. Homerun! Now we changed the cooking method because it's summer and too hot for the oven. We bbq'd the potatoes whole and then peeled. ouch! The electric mixer was a great idea. Added the walnuts after it was all mixed up and skipped the "back in the oven" step. They were still hot from the Q. I questioned the orange juice but it was surprisingly good. Everyone liked this one and I will make it again for sure! Thank you Terri

This are pretty tasty. They are too runny to rate a 5 star though. When I make them next time, I shall cut the orange juice and/or the butter.
I have found this is better (and easier) if one boils the sweet potatoes and jalapeno instead of baking. I also prefer it without the orange juice.

This are pretty tasty. They are too runny to rate a 5 star though. When I make them next time, I shall cut the orange juice and/or the butter.
I have found this is better (and easier) if one boils the sweet potatoes and jalapeno instead of baking. I also prefer it without the orange juice.

This was a delicious recipe! It took my potatoes about 2 hours to become tender enough to mash. I mashed them with a fork instead of a mixer so they had some texture to them. I also cut the butter by half and feel it could use even less if any Next time I will use more peppers.

It was pretty good! A nice switch from sweet versions. I left off the nuts because I forgot them. I also added some garlic salt. I'd probably add more jalapeno next time because mine was kind of small.

very good. Read recipe well, before starting; step "1" is actually 5 steps merged all together (for being poorly written, I give it a 4 star). I used 2 jalapenos, like other reviewers, but kept them in the oven 45 min, since they were on the larger side. This dish can tolerate extra baking in the oven to time with other sides or enteee.
my go to for Thanksgiving. Added 1 jalapeno.
This has become my favorite sweet potato recipe - sweet and heat is always a winner! The jalapeno gives it just the right amount of heat.

This is a go-to recipe at my house! It's a perfect flavor combination, zesty herb and buttery goodness, that ditches the tired brown sugar & cinnamon casseroles. I love to pair it with fish and other summer grilled meats. I like the exact butter amount, but the recipe still has plenty of flavor if you want to lighten the fat by cutting the butter in half. (I've made it both ways.) Roasting the jalapeno is essential! It's just the right amount of spice for a little heat but not too much to overpower the dish. And personally, we like a little extra cilantro, but as written, it's still noticeable flavor. I always make at least a double recipe: leftovers for at home, enough to go around at a small dinner party. As written, no changes, this is a true 5 star recipe. Thanks for sharing!

This was great if you are tired of too-sweet yam recipes. Gleaned from other reviews and my thoughts:
1) Jalapeños - had to add back the seeds because it wasn't hot enough. Next time I will roast two and skip the seeds for more flavor and a little more heat. 
2) Butter - use 1/8 cup. 
3) O.J. - used juice from an fresh orange along with some zest. may want to keep this to a minimum. 
4) Mash sweet potatoes rather than blend for more texture. 
5) Can roast sweet potatoes and pepper the day before to save time. 
6) Did not put back in oven, just to save time and I don't think it really needs it. No need to drizzle more butter at the end. It is good to go once mashed up. However roasting the walnuts in a dry skillet for a couple of minutes before topping the dish added to the flavor. 
7) Use more cilantro.
Goes great with pork and also with steak.
This dish is delicious and super easy with the perfect balance of savory and sweet with just the right kick!

This was amazing! I was curious of how cilantro, orange juice, and jalapeño would complement sweet potatoes, and I was amazed. Though I do confess that I wanted it a little sweeter, so I added about a tablespoon of maple syrup, which toned down the brightness of the orange juice. Served it as a side for meatloaf.

My family LOVED this and I am not even a sweet potatoe fan but the sweet and spicy was oh so yummy! My question is tho how do you peel the potatoes when they just come out of the oven?? I was burning my fingers! Maybe I'm reading instructions wrong?! And th cooking of the jalepeno part threw me off too- make sure to cook the jalepenos when the potatoes are cooking the first time or you will have to add another 20mins to your time. I just popped mine in the george foreman to get them cooked fast!
Nice accompaniment to Jay's Jerk Chicken.

Really zippy flavor! Definitely a repeat. Next time I will double it. Also, after roasting the jalepeno I took the seeds out to make it mild enough for the kids to eat. I still got the jalepeno flavor without too much bite. Also could halve the butter to cut down on fat, I didn't notice the difference.
